procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Can I come in this week?
documents.author: patient
documents.body: For the past week and a half I keep getting this feeling that food gets caught partway down, and sometimes a tight ache in my chest when it happens. It goes away on its own. Not an emergency I don't think but it's freaking me out a bit. Any chance of an appointment tomorrow after 3?

documents.title: Office Visit - Chest discomfort / dysphagia
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: 44F, about 10 days of intermittent episodes where food or a drink feels like it stops behind the sternum, sometimes with a tight discomfort in the same spot. Happens with solids and with liquids. Comes and goes on its own. Not exertional. No dyspnea, palpitations, diaphoresis. Denies weight loss, vomiting up undigested food, pain with swallowing, or any long-standing heartburn. No new meds. Work has been heavy this month.

PMH none. Meds none. NKDA. Never smoker. FH: father HTN, mother hypothyroid; no premature CAD she knows of.

O: vitals normal. Comfortable. Oropharynx clear, neck without mass or nodes, thyroid normal. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Chest wall nontender. Abdomen soft, no epigastric tenderness. No edema.
ECG in office: sinus rhythm, normal intervals, no ST-T changes.

A/P: Intermittent dysphagia to solids and liquids with retrosternal discomfort. Not anginal by history, ECG normal. Most likely reflux-related - trial of omeprazole 20 mg each morning before breakfast. Let me know in 3-4 weeks if not better; if no response, will get her to a specialist for a swallowing workup. Go to the ED for chest pain that is constant, exertional, or with shortness of breath, or if food truly will not pass.

documents.title: Omeprazole update
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Checking in like you asked. I've taken the omeprazole every morning for over 3 weeks and honestly no difference. Still getting the stuck feeling a few times a week, and very cold water seems to set it off. Do I keep taking it?

documents.title: RE: Omeprazole update
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thanks for the update. Since it hasn't helped at all, go ahead and stop the omeprazole. I'm sending a referral to ENT to look at the swallowing problem - their office will call you. If it gets worse before then, or food won't go down, call me.

documents.title: Referral to Otolaryngology
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Reason: 44F with ~5 weeks intermittent dysphagia to solids and liquids with retrosternal discomfort, no response to 3+ weeks of omeprazole 20 mg daily. Normal office ECG 1/27/25. Please evaluate. No medications. NKDA.

documents.title: Otolaryngology Consultation
documents.author: otolaryngology
documents.body:
Outside otolaryngology group - consultation letter
Date of visit: 02/28/2025
Re: Abigail Paquette, DOB 07/27/1980

Thank you for asking us to see Ms. Paquette, a 44-year-old project manager, for six weeks of swallowing trouble and chest discomfort.

She describes episodes in which a bite, or a sip, lodges at about the level of the mid-sternum. Some episodes bring a sharp, squeezing pain there that can travel through to her back. They last anywhere from a few minutes up to an hour, happen several times a week and usually pass without her doing anything. Very hot or very cold drinks can set them off, and she suspects pressure at work sometimes does as well. A course of omeprazole made no difference.

She has no meaningful past medical history and takes nothing regularly. Drug allergies: none known. No food allergy, no asthma. Family history notable for maternal hypothyroidism and paternal hypertension. She has never smoked and drinks one or two drinks a week.

Review of systems: no weight loss, no vomiting of undigested food, no odynophagia, no chronic heartburn.

Examination: vital signs stable. Well appearing. No pallor or other sign of anemia. Ears, nose and oral cavity normal. Oropharynx and neck without mass; no cervical lymphadenopathy; thyroid unremarkable. Heart and lung sounds normal.

Her ECG from your office on 01/27/2025, which I reviewed, is unremarkable.

Impression: The pattern - dysphagia to liquids as well as solids, a mid-chest level, thermal triggers, chest pain and no response to acid suppression - points to an esophageal motility disorder rather than an oropharyngeal or structural problem. I have recorded this as esophageal dysmotility.

Recommendations:
1. Gastroenterology evaluation for esophageal workup.
2. In the meantime, avoid very hot or very cold beverages and take smaller bites.
3. No ENT follow-up needed unless new throat or voice symptoms.

Thank you for involving our service.
Otolaryngology

orders.reason: Esophageal dysmotility, ENT recommends GI evaluation

documents.title: ENT letter
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Abby, I got the ENT letter. They think the esophagus muscle isn't squeezing in a coordinated way, which fits the cold-drink trigger and why omeprazole did nothing. Next step is GI. I've put the referral in. Their scheduling line can be slow, so let me know if you haven't heard in two weeks.

documents.title: RE: ENT letter
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Makes sense, thank you. Will keep an eye out for their call.

documents.title: GI referral on hold
documents.author: RN
documents.body:
Pt returned call re GI scheduling. States the swallowing episodes have quieted down over the past few weeks and she would rather hold off on GI for now given her work schedule. Advised to call if they return. Referral closed per pt request; PCP aware.

PCP addendum: fine. Low threshold to re-refer.

orders.reason: Recurrent dysphagia with regurgitation, esophageal dysmotility

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual. Also the swallowing problem is back.

Interval: the episodes from the winter faded out by April and she was fine over the summer. Starting about three weeks ago they returned - food and liquids hanging up mid-chest, and now some bringing back of undigested food after meals, which she did not have before. Occasional pressure-like pain behind the breastbone during episodes. Worse on high-stress days at work. Weight stable by our scale. No vomiting, no black stools or blood. No heartburn.

Meds: none. NKDA. Problem list: esophageal dysmotility (ENT impression 2/2025).
Social and family history unchanged.

ROS otherwise negative.

Exam: well. Vitals normal. HEENT benign, no cervical nodes, thyroid normal. Heart regular without murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, no organomegaly. No edema. Skin unremarkable.

A/P:
1. Esophageal dysmotility, symptoms recurrent with new regurgitation. Barium swallow ordered and GI referral placed again - she is ready to go this time. Same precautions: if food impacts and won't pass, ED.
2. Health maintenance: turned 45 this summer - discussed colon screening options, she prefers FIT; kit given. Mammogram order placed. Pap/HPV due next year. Labs: CBC, CMP, lipids, TSH. Flu vaccine today. PHQ-2 0.
RTC 1 yr, sooner as needed.

reports.text:
Indication: dysphagia to solids and liquids. Technique: single- and double-contrast esophagram with thin barium, followed by a barium tablet.
Oropharyngeal phase: normal bolus transit, no laryngeal penetration or aspiration.
Esophagus: on several swallows the distal esophagus shows intermittent non-propulsive contractions producing a corkscrew appearance, between which primary peristalsis is normal. The esophagus is not dilated. No stricture, ring, web, mass or diverticulum. Mucosa smooth. The barium tablet passed into the stomach without delay.
Gastroesophageal junction opens normally. No hiatal hernia. No reflux observed during the exam.
reports.conclusion: Intermittent corkscrew-like esophageal contractions, suggestive of a spastic motility disorder. No structural abnormality.
